segments.title: Chương 300: 0302 【Ai cũng là cao thủ】
segments.content:
Po Jie Animation had previously rented a civilian house for their office. After Chen Guiliang became a shareholder, they finally moved into a proper office building.

When it was founded in 2004, there were 14 people in total, all recent graduates or current university students.

After their first animated film flopped, five people left immediately. Three newcomers joined successively, and now the company had a total of 12 employees.

Outsourcing, outsourcing, and more outsourcing—many of the employees had grown numb to it.

If Chen Guiliang hadn't invested, the company probably would have disbanded in another two or three years at most.

"Welcome, President Chen, on your inspection tour." Wang Chenyu stepped forward to greet him with a grin.

This fellow was a graduate of the Beijing Film Academy's School of Animation. He was a bit slick in his speech and actions, but deep down, he was rather stubborn.

When he was asked to do the animation outsourcing for "Future Era," the specific requirements were all laid out clearly, but Wang Chenyu always insisted on adding his own personal touches.

Don't ask why.

The answer would be that it was more artistic, more perfect, more profound.

Some of the personal touches were well-added, and Chen Guiliang was willing to adopt them.

Some of them made Chen Guiliang want to hit someone.

Today, when Chen Guiliang came over, all the employees stopped their work.

Among these employees, most were graduates from the Beijing Film Academy and the Communication University of China, which were the two schools with the best animation programs in the capital at the time. There were also graduates from the Central Academy of Fine Arts, Peking University, Tsinghua University, and Renmin University of China.

"Let's have a meeting together," Chen Guiliang said.

There were only 12 people in total, and every one of them was a jack-of-all-trades. There was no need to leave anyone out.

The company didn't have a dedicated meeting room, so everyone dragged their chairs over and sat around Chen Guiliang, waiting for the meeting to start.

Chen Guiliang asked, "You all want to make animated films."

Everyone nodded silently.

Chen Guiliang asked again, "Do you know what the current market situation is for Chinese animated films?"

Most of them remained silent.

The meaning was obvious. Everyone knew what the situation was, but they still wanted to give it another shot.

Young people, right? They won't turn back until they hit a wall.

They had already hit a wall once, but they believed it was because they hadn't done a good job, so they wanted to go hit it again.

One employee couldn't help but say, "If all we do is take on outsourcing jobs or make children's animations, I might as well just join a game company. With my skills, working as an artist in a game company, wouldn't I make more money than doing animation?"

Wang Chenyu introduced, "This is Gu Kai, a graduate from Tsinghua's Academy of Arts & Design. His computer skills are very strong, and he also has a computer science degree from Tsinghua."

Tsinghua's Academy of Arts & Design had many majors; not all of them were about abstract art.

This Gu Kai had graduated from Tsinghua's Academy of Arts & Design's "Department of Information Art & Design" and also had a dual degree from Tsinghua's Computer Science department.

This person had also studied 3D animation production. If he went to a game company, he could definitely command a high salary. Yet, he chose to start a business with Wang Chenyu, toughing it out in a civilian house for three years. It was impossible to explain with anything other than dreams.

Another employee said, "Why is our company called Po Jie Animation? It's to break the boundaries and barriers of reality! It's true that the Chinese animated film industry isn't doing well, but that's only temporary. As long as we persist, we can succeed. The regular film market wasn't doing well before either, but isn't it getting better step by step these past few years? The annual box office has been continuously increasing. As the regular film market gets better step by step, animated films will also follow."

Wang Chenyu introduced, "This is Li Kaixuan, a graduate from the School of Animation and Digital Arts at the Communication University of China. Three years ago, he had already joined Shanda. When he heard we were starting a business to make animated films, he immediately resigned from Shanda and returned to Beijing."

Chen Guiliang could tell that the people before him would not be easily persuaded.

They wouldn't listen to anything he told them.

You bring up reality?

Then I have a more realistic option. I'll just go to a game company and end up making even more money!

Chen Guiliang approached it from another angle, "Have you ever thought that, setting aside the film's box office, your debut work itself has problems? I've seen that animated film, and I feel like the production team had too many ideas. All sorts of ideas and concepts were stuffed into it, ultimately destroying the overall structure and plot."

The crowd fell silent.

Because Chen Guiliang was speaking the truth.

They had also reviewed and analyzed it, and the conclusion they reached was: everyone in the company was too damn good, and everyone had too many ideas. When they couldn't convince each other, everyone's ideas were all crammed in. As a result, the animated film they produced looked quite good if you cut out any random few-minute clip, but when put together, it felt severely disjointed.

Wang Chenyu said, "We've already discussed this issue. If we make another animated film, we will coordinate with each other more seriously."

"Are you sure you can coordinate effectively?" Chen Guiliang asked with a smile.

"We can!" everyone guaranteed in unison.

Chen Guiliang said, "I believe you. Do you believe yourselves?"

Everyone smiled awkwardly.

Chen Guiliang said with a sigh, "With your team's current state, you're just not suited for making feature films. Even for making game cutscenes for me, I'd find you have too many ideas. Of course, one thing is undeniable. Your technical skills are truly incredible, and your visuals are top-notch. Some of the creative techniques for the animation shots are simply stunning, otherwise, I wouldn't have chosen you."

An employee said, "President Chen, just tell us directly what animation you want us to make."

Wang Chenyu introduced, "This is also a graduate from the CUC School of Animation, named Xiang Lei. He studied traditional Chinese painting before. The sweeping panoramic shot with shifting perspective in the opening animation of 'Future Era' was his design. Not just anyone can do that. It's rarely seen in Western animation and requires a foundation in Chinese painting to do well."

Chen Guiliang gave a thumbs-up, "That animation shot was particularly incredible. I sincerely admire it!"

Being praised by Chen Guiliang like that, Xiang Lei smiled a bit bashfully, but amidst the bashfulness, there was a hint of pride and self-confidence.

Chen Guiliang said, "You are all exceptionally talented and full of ideas. This is your strength, but also your team's weakness. You lack a decision-maker who can call the shots, a leader who can suppress the team members' ideas."

Wang Chenyu was very embarrassed.

He was nominally the boss of the animation company, but his relationship with the employees was more like that of brothers. When his brothers had ideas, he could only guide them, not forcefully suppress them.

Suppressing them wouldn't work anyway, unless he could convince them.

Chen Guiliang continued, "So, if you don't want to disband and still want to continue making animation, this team dynamic is not suitable for feature films. Once you make a feature, your internal problems will inevitably be exposed. It's best to make something that's a few minutes per episode, the shorter the better. If someone has a new idea, just make an episode specially for him."

"A few minutes per episode, you still want us to make children's animation, huh?" an employee sneered.

Wang Chenyu made another introduction.

Chen Guiliang retorted, "Who said it has to be children's animation? Can't adults watch it too?"

No one spoke again, just waiting for Chen Guiliang to give his specific suggestions.

Facing this group of opinionated and stubborn experts, Chen Guiliang didn't even dare to mention something like "Boonie Bears."

Once he said it, he would be looked down upon one hundred percent.

Have them animate "Those Things in the Ming Dynasty"? Or have them do "That Rabbit That Year Those Things"? That was also impossible.

Because both "Ming Dynasty" and "That Rabbit" were mainly narrative-driven, with no real requirements for visuals and camerawork. It wouldn't showcase the skills and creativity of these guys.

If they really did that, they might as well continue doing outsourcing for CCTV's "Stories of Chinese Virtues."

Chen Guiliang said, "Two ideas, you choose for yourselves."

"The first idea is to deconstruct 'Journey to the West' from the perspective of a grassroots demon. Let me tell you the first story, its name is 'A Little Demon's Summer.' There's a pig demon living at the very bottom of the hierarchy. Eating, sleeping, and patrolling the mountain is all his life consists of..."

"The second idea is a world of insects. There are two insects, Little Yellow and Little Red, who live in the sewers. Chewing gum, sausages, and pop cans that fall through the cracks of the sewer grate are all mysterious gifts that fall from the sky..."

"Both of these ideas can be made to appeal to all ages. And the episodes are short, so you can mess around with them however you want. Whoever has a creative idea can make it into an episode, and everyone else will fully cooperate."

"When you finally understand how to compromise and forbear, when you know how to cooperate with others, only then will I allow you to make a feature film. If anyone feels this doesn't meet their expectations, they can resign directly."

Xiang Lei, the one with a foundation in Chinese painting, was the first to speak. "I think we should choose the first one. There are countless demons in 'Journey to the West,' so we can also design countless grassroots little demons. The story of the pilgrimage is just the background of their lives; they have their own joys and sorrows. This animated series isn't about the pilgrimage, but a reflection of modern people's lives."

Gu Kai, the Tsinghua and Peking University graduate skilled in 3D animation, said, "I choose the second one. A group of insects living in the sewers can also be a microcosm of human society. And, it can be more exaggerated, more childlike, and more dramatic than directly portraying humans."

These guys all made their choices one by one; 7 chose the first one, and 5 chose the second.

Then, they started bickering among themselves, completely forgetting Chen Guiliang was there.

Wang Chenyu was extremely embarrassed.

His team really had problems. Every single one was an expert. They usually joked around and got along great, but the moment they encountered a work-related issue, they would argue endlessly.

Chen Guiliang had only told the story of "A Little Demon's Summer," which basically set the tone. They were free to make up the other stories.

"Larva" was even simpler, two to three minutes an episode, allowing for complete creative freedom.

In fact, "Larva" was better suited for the market.

Each episode was very short, making it flexible for broadcasting, and children's acceptance would also be higher. They could totally cooperate with television stations.

The series of grassroots demon stories from "Journey to the West" belonged to the category of long-form animated shorts, with each episode being twenty to thirty minutes. If it were broadcast on a children's programming channel, one episode would have to be split up to be shown.

With the scene turning into a chaotic argument, Chen Guiliang could only step forward and make the final call. "How about this. First, we'll do 'A Little Demon's Summer.' Treat it as an animated short film. You can even take it to film festivals to win awards and fulfill your artistic pursuits. Then, we'll do 'Larva,' and cooperate with major television stations for broadcast. When you have time and new ideas, you can work on the second episode of the grassroots demon series."

No one objected to this solution.

Wang Chenyu followed Chen Guiliang out of the company. "President Chen, I want to hire a few more people. After all, we still have to do the cutscene animations for 'Future Era.'"

"Go ahead and hire, but for now, don't let the total number of employees exceed 18. When you can make money without relying on outsourcing, then come talk to me about expanding," Chen Guiliang said.

Wang Chenyu said solemnly, "'Larva' will definitely make money."

Being able to say something like this proved that Wang Chenyu understood the market; it was just that he didn't want to cater to it.

Chen Guiliang was running a social networking site and a game company, and he also invested in a video website, a music website, and an animation company. This wasn't him taking a scattered, hit-or-miss approach; he was laying out a business strategy.

All these things could be integrated together in the future.

He even had to find a suitable time to invest in and open a film and television company. In the future, film and television copyrights would be too expensive, so expensive that video websites couldn't afford them. It would be more cost-effective to just invest in and produce films and TV series themselves.

After leaving Po Jie Animation, a gust of strong wind carrying sand and dust blew over.

Damn, the sandstorm weather is here again
